summary:
Verified: 23/23 companies, 24/24 facilities, 28/28 flows, 5/5 financial_links (controls: none in this layer). Verdicts: 78 publish, 8 publish_flagged, 0 reject.

Every SEC filing cited (TSMC 20-F, ASML 20-F, Intel 10-K, GlobalFoundries 20-F, KLA 10-K, Lam 10-K) was confirmed as a real, correctly-dated EDGAR filing and downloaded directly; every quoted passage across all four filings' company/facility/flow/financial_link evidence was checked verbatim against the downloaded text and matched exactly, including all fab-table rows (start year / wafer size / most advanced node) and every customer-concentration percentage. SEC's Archives host blocks plain automated User-Agents with a 403 'Undeclared Automated Tool' page even when the UA string is descriptive; adding ordinary browser Accept/Accept-Language/Connection headers (still with a descriptive, non-personal UA, no invented email) reliably got past it. EDGAR's full-text search API mis-tokenizes curly apostrophes and produced two false negatives (ASML's and Lam's quotes) that were verbatim in the actual filings -- worth remembering for future layers.

TSMC's website and press-release pages (flagged by the analyst as fetched through a text-rendering proxy) were re-fetched live directly for this review; every quote matched verbatim, including the full 2025 Supplier Award winner list. TSMC's investor-relations PDFs (AR ch1, ch5) sit behind a Cloudflare JS challenge that blocks curl entirely regardless of headers; a browser-rendering fetch path recovered the actual PDFs and both quotes checked out verbatim. One incidental finding: AR ch1 contains an uncited-but-relevant sentence giving JASM's second fab a planned node (3nm) and ESMC Dresden a product focus (automotive/industrial specialty tech) -- both facilities currently carry products: [] in the research file. This is a gap, not an error, and is called out per-entity above for the analyst to consider filling with a proper citation; I did not add the claim myself since evidence for those specific fields wasn't in the entity's own evidence[] and adding it would go beyond correcting an existing field.

Inferred ASML-EUV flows to specific fabs (TSMC Fab 18/20/22, Samsung Hwaseong/Pyeongtaek, Intel Oregon/Arizona/Ireland) all have honest inference_notes that explicitly disclose no document ties the specific tool to the specific site -- these are sound, properly-labeled 'inferred' flows and are publish_flagged (dashed-line) rather than rejected, consistent with the AGENTS.md worked example for this exact pattern.

Samsung's DS Division supplier evidence (Siltronic, SK Siltron, Soulbrain, DongWoo Fine-Chem) covers memory and foundry combined, and every description already discloses this explicitly ('Not split by memory vs foundry fab') -- no correction needed; none of the four supplier flows target a specific Samsung facility, so there is no foundry-specific overclaim to catch.

Revenue-concentration financial_links (TSMC, Intel, GlobalFoundries, SMIC, Samsung) are all self-referencing (from = to = the disclosing company) because the filings do not name the customers. Every percentage and fiscal year was checked character-for-character against the downloaded filings and all matched exactly -- no corrections needed.

Two stale-status flags, both requested by the brief: (1) fac:samsung-taylor -- the only Tier 1/2 source is a Dec 2024 NIST award page; re-fetched live today (2026-09-28) it is unchanged and still targets 2030 completion, and Samsung's FY2025 business report gives no more specific update, so 'under_construction' is plausible but unconfirmed by any fresher document -- publish_flagged rather than corrected. (2) fac:samsung-pyeongtaek-foundry -- the sole facility-specific source is a May 2020 release whose own target completion date (2H 2021) is now ~5 years past; Samsung's FY2025 report confirms Pyeongtaek remains active with unspecified 'new line construction' but does not confirm the original EUV line's current status. 'under_construction' is very likely stale (the line almost certainly went operational years ago) but I could not find a Tier 1/2 document stating that explicitly, so I flagged rather than force-corrected the status without a supporting quote -- recommend the analyst locate a 2024-2026 Samsung disclosure that states Pyeongtaek foundry-line status directly.

By contrast, TSMC Arizona Fab 21 phase 2/3 and Intel Ohio -- also named by the brief as staleness candidates -- checked out as CURRENT, not stale: TSMC's own FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-04-16, the newest source in this file) directly confirms phase 2 construction is 'ongoing' and phase 3 'commenced in 2025', and Intel's FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-01-23) directly confirms Ohio construction has been 'further slowed down' -- both are the most recent possible Tier 1 statements on those facilities, so no flag was needed.

Rejected: none. Corrections applied: none (no wrong quote, number, date, name, or status was found anywhere in this file; the two stale-status concerns could not be corrected without inventing an unsupported value, so they were flagged instead per the brief's explicit instruction).
